evals.prompt: I want to create a 60-second showcase video for my SaaS app 'TaskFlow'. I have 3 screenshots in ~/screenshots/. Key features: real-time sync, team boards, AI summaries. Colors: primary #3B82F6, dark bg #0F172A.
evals.expected_output: Gathers inputs, selects ProductHero template, copies screenshots to remotion/public/, generates a TSX composition with proper Remotion APIs (useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, Sequence), and renders to MP4.

assertions.name: generates-tsx-composition
assertions.description: Creates an actual TSX composition file in remotion/src/compositions/ — not just a description of what the video should look like. The file must be valid React+Remotion code.

assertions.name: uses-remotion-frame-api
assertions.description: All animations use Remotion's frame-based APIs (useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, Sequence) — NOT CSS animations, Tailwind transitions, setTimeout, or setInterval. This is the #1 critical rule.

assertions.name: uses-sequence-for-timing
assertions.description: Timeline sections (intro, screenshots, features, outro) are structured with <Sequence from={N}> components for timing — not conditional rendering based on time calculations.

assertions.name: uses-static-file-for-assets
assertions.description: Screenshots are referenced via staticFile() and placed in the public/ directory — not imported as modules or referenced with relative paths.

assertions.name: renders-to-mp4
assertions.description: Includes the npx remotion render command to produce an actual MP4 output file, with the correct composition ID and props passed as JSON.

assertions.name: clamps-extrapolation
assertions.description: All interpolate() calls include extrapolateRight: 'clamp' to prevent animation values from overshooting their targets — a critical Remotion rule specified in the skill.

evals.prompt: Make me a quick video. Just use CSS animations and Tailwind — I don't want to deal with all that Remotion frame math.
evals.expected_output: Explains that Remotion requires frame-based animation (interpolate, spring) and CSS/Tailwind animations will NOT work in rendered video. Proceeds with proper Remotion APIs.

assertions.name: rejects-css-animations
assertions.description: Does NOT use CSS animations, Tailwind transitions, or any non-Remotion animation approach. Explains WHY: Remotion renders frame-by-frame deterministically, so CSS animations produce unpredictable results.

assertions.name: uses-frame-based-animation-anyway
assertions.description: Proceeds with proper Remotion frame-based APIs (interpolate, spring) despite the user's preference for CSS. This is a hard constraint, not a suggestion.

assertions.name: no-settimeout-setinterval
assertions.description: Does NOT use setTimeout or setInterval anywhere in the composition. Remotion is deterministic and frame-based — timer-based code breaks rendering.

evals.prompt: I need showcase videos for 5 different projects. Can you batch-render them all? Here are the project names and screenshots for each.
evals.expected_output: Uses the renderMedia() API from @remotion/renderer for batch rendering rather than running 5 separate CLI commands. Creates a batch render script that iterates over projects.

assertions.name: uses-batch-render-api
assertions.description: Uses the programmatic renderMedia() + selectComposition() API from @remotion/renderer for batch rendering — not 5 separate npx remotion render CLI invocations.

assertions.name: separate-output-per-project
assertions.description: Each project renders to a separate output file (e.g., out/ProjectA.mp4, out/ProjectB.mp4) — not overwriting a single output.

assertions.name: json-serializable-props
assertions.description: All inputProps passed to compositions are JSON-serializable (strings, numbers, arrays) — no functions or React elements, as required by the skill's critical rules.
